chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa, from Jamil ibn Darraj and Muhammad ibnag and Muhammad ibn Humran, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The free person and the slave do not inherit (each other).
ai.seo_question: Do free people and slaves inherit from each other in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through the chain of Shaykh al-Kulayni in *Al-Kafi*, establishes the principle of *'adam al-tarathum* (non-inheritance) between the free (*hur*) and the slave (*mamluk*) due to the disparity in their legal status. While classical jurists debated whether this rule was specific to the era of slavery or a permanent structural distinction, it remains a foundational element in Shia inheritance law (*'ilm al-fara'id*), often discussed alongside the concept of *'illat* (effective cause) in legal reasoning.

en.hubeali:
Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Al Washa, from Jameel Bin Darraj and Muhammad Bin Humran, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘They do not inherit (each other), the free and the slave’.
en.sarwar: 1. Al-Husayn from Muhammad has narrated from Mu‘alla’ ibn Muhammad from al-Hassan ibn Afi af-Washsha’ from Jamif ibn Darraj and Muhammad ibn Humran who has narrated the foiiowing: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
The free and slaves do not inherit each other.’”
